extra.message: The /ping route concatenates the user-controlled 'id' query parameter directly into a shell command passed to child_process.exec(). An attacker can inject arbitrary OS commands (e.g. '?id=127.0.0.1;ls') enabling remote command execution on the server.

The /eval route passes the attacker-controlled query parameters 'id' and 'id2' directly to eval() (result = eval(id + id2)). This allows arbitrary server-side JavaScript execution (code injection / RCE), e.g. '?id=require('child_process').execSync('id')'.

The /api/users login handler builds a MongoDB query from unvalidated request fields. The password is JSON.parse()'d whenever it contains '{' (lines 28-32) and the resulting object (and the equally unvalidated email field from the JSON body) is used as a Mongo query selector. An attacker can supply {"password": {"$ne": ""}} to bypass authentication entirely and log in as any user, or inject arbitrary query operators (NoSQL injection / authentication bypass).

The /getdata route JSON.parse()'s the attacker-controlled 'id' query parameter and passes the resulting object directly to a MongoDB find() selector ({ id: id }). An attacker can inject query operators such as '?id={"$ne":null}' to dump arbitrary user records, or '?id={"$gt":""}' to match all documents (NoSQL injection). A malformed id also throws an unhandled exception.

The /a6_misconfig route JSON.parse()'s the attacker-controlled body field 'accountno' and uses the resulting object directly in a MongoDB find() selector. Posting {"accountno": {"$ne": null}} (or any operator object) lets an attacker bypass the intended lookup and retrieve arbitrary records (NoSQL injection).

The /insecure_dor route returns bank account records from the a5_insecure_dor collection for any caller-supplied 'accountno' with no authentication or ownership check. An attacker can enumerate account numbers (1001-1010) to read other users' account names and account types — an Insecure Direct Object Reference / broken access control. Because accountno comes from a JSON-parsed body it is also injectable as a Mongo operator object.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The a3_xss_reflected controller marks the server-returned, user-influenced 'search' value from GET /xss_r (which reflects the unsanitized 'id' query parameter at index.js:170) as trusted HTML via $sce.trustAsHtml and binds it with ng-bind-html (a7_xss_reflected.html). Because the value is echoed back without encoding and rendered without the Angular sanitizer, an attacker-supplied payload is executed in the victim's browser (reflected/DOM XSS).

The /a3sensitive route performs no authentication or authorization and returns full user documents (including the 'password' field of every user in the collection) for any caller-supplied 'id'. Anyone can read stored credentials by querying arbitrary ids (Sensitive Data Exposure / missing access control).

The /a3sensitive_header route serializes and returns the client's entire request header set to the browser. This can expose sensitive header values (e.g. Cookie/session tokens when this endpoint is called from other origins via a browser) and is an unnecessary information disclosure.

The /a6_misconfig route sends raw MongoDB driver error objects back to the client via res.json(err) (also at line 188). These errors can leak internal database/server details (connection strings, stack traces, collection internals) to unauthenticated attackers (sensitive information in error messages).

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: express-session is configured with a hardcoded, guessable secret ("Your secret key") and no cookie security options (no 'secure', 'httpOnly' is left to the library default, no session store hardening). An attacker who knows the default secret can forge/decrypt session cookies to impersonate any logged-in user.
The /api/users login handler writes the parsed search object (containing the plaintext email and password supplied by the client) to the server console, exposing credentials in log output.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File
